prompt: Implement mergeSorted to combine two already-sorted int arrays into one sorted array using the classic two-pointer merge, without sorting from scratch.
explanation: The two-pointer merge keeps one index into each input array and repeatedly copies the smaller of the two current elements into the output, advancing only that pointer. When one input runs out, the remainder of the other is copied straight across. This is the O(n + m) heart of merge sort and never needs to re-sort anything.
hints: The result array has exactly a.length + b.length slots -- allocate it up front.
Keep three indexes: i into a, j into b, and out into the result. Compare a[i] with b[j] each step.
After the main loop one array may still have elements left; copy its tail with a simple while loop.
